share_verdict: Steamed rice and jaggery, once. Fried, and full of mawa, now.

source.text: The modaka — a steamed rice-flour dumpling stuffed with coconut and jaggery — is an old festival sweet described across Sanskrit literature; the Mānasollāsa (12th CE) lists modaka among its festival foods. It survives as Maharashtra's ukadiche modak and the South's kozhukattai.
source.century: Pre-12th CE, with the Mānasollāsa description 12th CE

ingredients.name: rice flour
ingredients.function: the steamed shell; ground rice makes a soft, pliable dough that sets firm and translucent when steamed

ingredients.name: fresh coconut
ingredients.function: the body of the filling — fat, bulk and the sweetness-carrier

ingredients.name: jaggery
ingredients.function: the sweetener and binder of the filling; melted, it sets the coconut into a soft mass

ingredients.name: ghee
ingredients.function: a little in the dough keeps the shell supple, and it greases the mould and hands for shaping

method_reconstructed: Boil water with a little ghee and salt, stir in the rice flour off the heat, cover, and rest, then knead to a smooth, soft dough while warm.
Cook the grated coconut with the jaggery over low heat until it comes together, then fold in the crushed cardamom.
Shape a ball of dough into a cup, fill it, and pinch the top closed into the pleated peak.
Steam the modak for ten to twelve minutes until the shell turns glossy and translucent.
contested_points: Modaka is an old, pan-Indian word that split into two lines: the steamed rice-flour dumpling recorded here (Maharashtra's ukadiche modak, the Tamil kozhukattai) and the rolled sweet ball that became the modern laddu, which has its own record.
Whether the Mānasollāsa's modaka is specifically the steamed form is not settled — the term covers both — so this record claims no verse.

changed.to: refined sugar, and in shop sweets mawa (khoya) or chocolate
changed.driver: refined sugar is cheaper and more uniform than jaggery, and mithai shops built mawa- and chocolate-filled modak as premium novelties

changed.to: fried shells and refined-flour or ready-mix wrappers
changed.driver: frying and ready shells keep longer and read as richer than the plain steamed dumpling

ingredients: 1 tsp ghee, plus more for the mould
steps: Cook the coconut with the jaggery over low heat until it holds together, then stir in the cardamom and cool.
Boil one cup of water with the ghee and salt. Off the heat, stir in the rice flour, cover, and rest two minutes.
Knead the warm dough smooth. Grease your palms, shape a small cup, fill it, and pinch the top into pleats.
Steam ten to twelve minutes until the shells turn glossy and translucent.
Eat warm with a little more ghee — the shell is soft, the filling barely sweet and all coconut.

verification.note: Seed record, split from the former combined modaka/laddu entry so the steamed dumpling and the rolled sweet ball are no longer conflated. Not yet checked against a printed edition, so no verse or page is claimed.
